hero_kpi_rationale: Cloud revenue is Oracle's primary growth driver, with an accelerated migration of the existing customer base to the cloud, notably through OCI and OCA, positioning the company at the heart of the cloud infrastructure and AI wave.
company_description: Oracle Corporation offers products and services that address enterprise information technology environments worldwide. Its Oracle cloud software as a service offering include various cloud software applications, including Oracle Fusion cloud enterprise resource planning ERP, Oracle Fusion cloud enterprise performance management EPM, Oracle Fusion cloud supply chain and manufacturing management SCM, Oracle Fusion cloud human capital management HCM, and NetSuite applications suite, Oracle Health applications, as well as Oracle Fusion Sales, Service, and Marketing. The company also offers cloud-based industry solutions for various industries; Oracle cloud license and on-premise license; and Oracle license support services. In addition, it provides cloud and license business' infrastructure technologies, such as the Oracle Database and MySQL Database; Java, a software development language; and middleware, including development tools and others. The company's cloud and license business' infrastructure technologies also comprise cloud-based compute, storage, and networking capabilities; and Oracle autonomous database, as well as AI, Internet-of-Things, machine learning, digital assistant

kpis.name: Cloud Share of Revenue
kpis.explanation: Cloud services revenue as a percentage of total revenue.
kpis.description: Cloud services revenue accounted for 43% of total revenue in 2025, up from 37% in 2024 and 32% in 2023, showing increasing adoption of Oracle cloud.
kpis.signal: Cloud share of total revenue is rising sharply.

kpis.name: Cloud and License Share of Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the cloud and license segment (including cloud services, license support, cloud license and on-premise license) as a percentage of total revenue.
kpis.description: Cloud and license represented 86% of total revenue in 2025, up from 84% in 2024, indicating a stronger focus on high-margin activities.

kpis.name: Gross Margin (estimated)
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of sales (estimate).
kpis.description: Oracle posts a high gross margin, consistent with its software and cloud model. Estimated value not available in the provided 10-K.
kpis.signal: High gross margin typical of cloud software vendors.

kpis.name: Operating Margin (estimated)
kpis.description: Estimated at around 35%, in line with major software publishers like Oracle that benefit from economies of scale and recurring revenue. Value not available in the provided 10-K.
kpis.signal: Solid operating margin for a software vendor.

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of revenue, estimated)
kpis.explanation: R&D expenses as a percentage of revenue (estimate).
kpis.description: Oracle continues to invest heavily in R&D to develop its cloud and AI offerings, notably via OCI and its cloud applications. Estimated value not available in the provided 10-K.
kpis.signal: Sustained investment in cloud and AI innovation.

kpis.name: Hardware Share of Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the hardware segment as a percentage of total revenue.
kpis.description: The hardware segment represented 5% of total revenue in 2025, down from 6% in 2024, reflecting the transition to cloud.
kpis.signal: Declining weight of hardware in the product mix.

kpis.description: Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Revenue of $57.399 billion in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of $12.443 billion in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $1.0 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $4.743 billion in the latest year.

kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 38.1% in the latest year.

risks.title: FX Risk on Revenue
risks.summary: Foreign currency fluctuations can significantly reduce revenue reported in US dollars.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is clearly quantified in the Sensitivity Analysis section, with a potential loss of $2,379M in case of a 10% drop in exchange rates. The language emphasizes the significant impact on consolidated revenue. The company has major international exposure, which reinforces severity. Heavy weighting for macro risks tied to currencies. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: FX Transaction Risk
risks.summary: Foreign currency transactions generate gains or losses not fully hedged by forward contracts.
risks.score_rationale: The text describes significant exposures in multiple major currencies (euro, yen, pound sterling, etc.) and at-risk intercompany transactions. Use of forward contracts is mentioned as a mitigation, but the program may be suspended. The impact on results is direct and recorded in non-operating items. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Future Currency Volatility
risks.summary: The international scale of operations exposes Oracle to future currency volatility that is difficult to forecast.
risks.score_rationale: The company warns that increased currency volatility could occur in the future, with uncertain amounts and timing. This indicates a prospective risk that is not quantified but acknowledged as possible due to the scale of international operations. Less severe because anticipated and partially hedged. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Uncertain Tax Positions
risks.summary: Complex tax interpretations, notably on transfer pricing, could result in significant adjustments.
risks.score_rationale: The audit report flags uncertain tax positions as a 'Critical Audit Matter', the highest level of attention. This concerns complex judgments on transfer pricing and interpretation of tax laws. The involvement of tax specialists in the audit reinforces the severity of the risk. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Inherent Limitations of Controls
risks.summary: No control system can guarantee the complete absence of errors or fraud due to inherent limitations.
risks.score_rationale: The internal controls section explicitly acknowledges that control systems cannot guarantee the absence of error or fraud. This risk is systemic and inherent to any business, but mentioned here with cautious language. Moderate severity as it is a universal limitation, but acknowledged by management. (default score, to be refined)

ai_positioning.summary: Oracle is gradually integrating AI into its cloud applications and infrastructure, notably through OCI and its intelligent application offerings, without positioning AI as a standalone flagship product.
evidence: Growth in cloud deals including AI features
Investments in Ampere Computing for cloud and AI infrastructure
Development of new cloud features with unspecified updates including AI enhancements
